blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built from the BC Strata Property Act pages, the BC property transfer tax page and the CRA new-housing rebate guide named under Sources, read November 1, 2026. Not legal advice.

These BC points apply to every duplex or half-duplex purchase on this site, whichever area it is in. They are written once here; each area page covers only the duplex form and local rules specific to that area.
A duplex and a half duplex are not the same thing

A duplex is one building with two dwelling units, usually on one lot under one title. A half duplex is one of the two units sold on its own. In BC that happens in two legal forms only: a strata duplex, where the pair is a two-lot strata plan and each half is a strata lot, or a fee-simple half duplex, where the parcel was subdivided so each half sits on its own lot. A duplex that was never strata-divided or subdivided cannot be bought by the half: the whole building and lot sell together.

A strata half duplex is bought like any strata lot. Ask for the Form B information certificate, the bylaws and rules, the financial statements, the insurance and the meeting minutes. Depreciation reports run on a five-year cycle for stratas with five or more lots, so a two-lot strata falls below that threshold on lot count alone; still ask what reports the strata holds. The minimum contingency-reserve contribution is 10% of the operating budget. Rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022.

Only a 55+ age bylaw is valid in a BC strata. A strata may restrict residents to age 55 or older under sections 123.1 and 123.2 of the Strata Property Act, and a bylaw set below 55 has been invalid since November 24, 2022. Nothing on this site presents a duplex as age-restricted unless the strata bylaw says so.
Fee-simple half duplex: subdivision and the party wall

Splitting a duplex lot into two titles needs subdivision approval through the municipality’s Approving Officer, against the zoning minimums in force. The two owners are tied together by the registered party-wall or easement agreement on both titles, so read both titles and the agreement before you remove subjects.
Small-scale multi-unit housing does not split a duplex

BC’s small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) zoning lets many single-detached and duplex lots hold more units, including suites and coach houses where the municipality allows them. More units on a lot is not the same as separate titles: a separately owned half still needs a strata plan or a subdivision. Each municipality’s own rules are summarized on its area pages.

BC property transfer tax is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2,000,000, 3% above $2,000,000, and a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000. On a fully residential purchase with no exemption, $800,000 is $14,000, $1,000,000 is $18,000 and $2,000,000 is $38,000. A half duplex is taxed on its own purchase price as its own transfer. First-time buyer and newly built exemptions have their own tests, so check the Province’s page for your purchase.

GST and the federal new-housing rebates apply to new housing. A resale duplex or half duplex is not new housing for those rebates. If you are buying a newly built half duplex, the contract should state whether GST is included, and who claims any rebate.

faq.a: A duplex is one building with two units, normally on one lot and one title. A half duplex is one of the two units sold separately, which in BC only happens as a strata lot in a two-lot strata plan or as a fee-simple lot created by subdivision.
faq.q: What is the difference between a duplex and a half duplex in BC?

faq.a: Only if the two halves already have separate titles, either as strata lots or as subdivided fee-simple lots. If the duplex sits on one lot under one title, the whole building and lot sell together.
faq.q: Can I buy just one half of a duplex?

faq.a: The five-year depreciation-report cycle applies to stratas with five or more lots, so a two-lot strata is below that threshold on lot count. Ask the strata what reports it holds anyway.
faq.q: Does a two-lot strata need a depreciation report?

faq.a: No. It allows more units on a lot, not separate ownership. A separately titled half needs a strata plan or a subdivision.
faq.q: Does small-scale multi-unit housing zoning let me split a duplex into two titles?

faq.a: No. Rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022, and only a 55+ age bylaw is valid.
faq.q: Can a strata ban rentals or set an under-55 age limit?

faq.a: On the half’s own purchase price using the standard tiers: 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above that, and a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000, unless an exemption applies.
faq.q: How is property transfer tax calculated on a half duplex?
